Project Status Update – Cloud Migration
Project: Cloud Migration Phase 2
Date: September 1, 2026
The engineering team has completed 70% of the migration. The remaining production databases must be
migrated before September 20, 2026.
Tasks:
 Ravi will prepare the database migration checklist by September 5, 2026.
 Priya will complete load testing before September 10, 2026.
 The DevOps team will update the production rollback plan by September 12, 2026.
Risks:
 The current migration timeline is aggressive because database testing has not started.
 Production downtime may exceed the planned two-hour maintenance window if rollback testing fails.
 A dependency on the external security vendor may delay final approval.
Decisions:
 The team decided to use a phased migration instead of a single weekend cutover.
 The production release will proceed only after successful rollback testing.
 Daily progress meetings will continue until migration completion.

Project Atlas Status Report

Project Status
Project Atlas is developing a customer support analytics system. The planned release date is 30 October
2026. The authentication module is complete, while the analytics dashboard is 85% complete.
Current Issue
The reporting API is unstable and is delaying integration testing.
Tasks
Riya must stabilize the reporting API by 15 September 2026. Aman must complete dashboard testing by 18
September 2026. The QA team must prepare regression test cases by 20 September 2026.
Risks
If the reporting API remains unstable, the planned release may be delayed. The external analytics provider
has also not confirmed the final API version.
Decisions
The team decided to release the analytics dashboard first and move advanced reporting features to Phase 2.

cleanedText:
Cloud Service Contract Review

Background
The company is evaluating a three-year cloud data-processing contract with a service provider.
Findings
The proposal offers a 12% cost reduction. However, service availability is guaranteed at only 99.5%, while the
internal requirement is 99.9%.
Tasks
The legal team must request stronger data-loss clauses. The compliance team must verify backup-data
locations. Procurement must negotiate a 99.9% availability commitment.
Risks
The lower availability guarantee may affect business operations. Data-loss penalties are unclear. Backup
data may be stored in another geographic region, creating compliance concerns.
Decisions
Management must decide whether to sign the contract before 25 September 2026 or continue negotiations.
